fixes.explanation: That one's a stretch, friend, since the psalm never mentions Egypt here. God says, "So I gave them up to their stubborn hearts to follow their own devices." (Psalm 81:12) The verse before says, "But My people would not listen to Me, and Israel would not obey Me." (Psalm 81:11) So He doesn't send them anywhere. He leaves them with their stubborn hearts and their own plans, which is what "their own devices" means.

Reasonable guess, friend, but the psalm doesn't mention a prophet here. God says, "So I gave them up to their stubborn hearts to follow their own devices." (Psalm 81:12) Right before it, He says, "But My people would not listen to Me…" (Psalm 81:11) So He lets them follow their stubborn hearts and their own plans, which is what "their own devices" means.

problems.problem: Going their own way instead of God's ways restates the verse without explaining what following their own devices means.
Going their own way with stubborn hearts leading restates the verse without explaining what following their own devices means.
